entry.text: Schedule's simple - Mondays and Fridays are yours. That's all I trust you with.
Monday didn't kill you. Let's see what Friday does.
Have fun.
(Oh. Good morning. That's Erika. Same bright grin as in school, like nothing bad ever sticks.)
(Back then she was the only one who gave a shit about me.)
(...Or at least I hope that part wasn't theatre.)
Gail! Oh my god, it really is you.
I totally thought you'd leave Larris again right after the funeral. Like- poof. Stormy beach, dramatic coat, no forwarding address.
But then Father Jean-Noël said he saw you in here, and I thought he was joking, but look at that. You didn't leave.
I still have to deal with the flat. Paperwork, dust, old things.
Oh... Right.
Sorry, Gail.
...But since when are you a cashier? I always pictured you ending up in a lighthouse, or something like that. Hallucinating mermaids and fighting with gulls and stuff.

response.text: Damn. Some kids get silver spoons, you got Félix. Condolences.
Uh oh, smells like denial in here.
That's my girl.

entry.text: Anyway, point is... I'm glad you're back.

response.text: Yeah. Whatever happened before the organ gave that last cry and keeled over. I can't pin it yet, but it smells off.
Too many details that don't sit right, and too many people acting off about it.
Ha. Where do I even start...
They covered it with cloth, you know? Pulled it so tight like nobody's supposed to peek. Which, obviously, made me peek.
And what was under there? Remember, the official story is our sensitive, dramatic organ just... chose the boring path of wear and tear.
Yeah, well, which "natural cause" rips a whole bunch of keys straight out? A heatwave so bad they ran away together? Please.
...By the way. Do you know who's helping out at the church these days?
What, it's not just Father Jean-Noël and the nuns running that place?
Oh, then I'll let you find out. It's more fun that way.

Yeah. All the church crowd dodging the topic and acting like the organ went and made some little silent protest. And the music lads, lurking there after dark like smugglers. And, mm... other stuff, you get the idea.
And then everyone wonders why I get curious...

wby.text: Hmm... okay, so I finished school last year. Now I write little pieces for the paper, you know, like local stuff, whatever happens in the town, basically.
(No wonder the paper's all over the place these days.)
Plus, I sometimes send spooky stories to this underground zine in Villebourg.
Oh! And I got a scooter. Finally. It's yellow and has zero horsepower, but I love it.
...I think about leaving too, sometimes. Traveling. Maybe doing real journalism. But... I guess life here hasn't pissed me off quite enough yet.

seals.text: Yeah... White puffballs, speckled blobs, silly whiskery noses... My sweet big floppers.

You know, they showed up a bit early this year, and on such an odd night. First seal appeared, all round and confused. Full moon overhead. I guess it was the night right before Viviane's funeral, which is probably not connected, but also... it just felt off.
*giggle* Sorry, I just... the whole timing was insane. First the moon, then the seal, then the fuss in the church and our sad little organ falling apart. What a night.

end.text: So... Did you want to buy something, or...?
No. Just wanted to see you before work.

after.text: Before leaving, Erika paused and pulled a piece of paper from her pocket. She stared at it for a moment, then tore it up nervously and dropped the scraps into the bin before hurrying out.

response.text: (...I'll take a look when it's quiet.)

entry.text: Good morning. What a beautiful day it is today.
No parcels or letters for this address. Just here for the blue Jesuses and two toffees, please.

entry_decorOrdered.text: Good morning. What a beautiful day it is today.
I've got a parcel for the shop. Could you sign here?
Thanks. And I'll take the blue Jesuses and two toffees, please.

response.text: And you're already back in town, aren't you?
...Of course I'm back. A little "mild head injury and mud exposure" won't stop me or my bike.
Lost the bell again, though. Shame. I liked that one.
Oh, blue JC. Jesus Christ, a lot of people call them that.
You know what those letters actually stand for?

options.text: Probably Jean-Claude or some other name

response.text: Okay. Sounds legit.
I like this version too.
Come on, they're not that bad.

wrong_items_jesuses.text: JC. Blue packet. And two toffee candies. Wrapper with cow spots.

checkout.text: Thanks. Back to work. Would be nice not to meet the pavement today.

after_decorOrdered.text: (Alright, mystery parcel. Let's see what's inside.)

options.text: Looks like it came out of a bin
Ugly enough to feel like home

after_decorOrdered.text: There was no sender's name. Just a small card tucked inside: "From your trusted supplier."

entry.text: (Oh look. Another old friend showed up.)
(Shared lice, first cigarettes and years of being horrible to each other.)
(You know. Normal childhood friendship.)

response.text: Hey. Yeah, I heard you were back.
Came to say hi to your dear old friend?
Obviously. Couldn't fucking wait.
I'm here to buy Jean-Noël his mugwort Fleuries. That's all.
What, still haven't learned to form a thought?
No, I didn't end up in jail like you all expected.
Yeah, that's a rosary you're staring at.
Cool one. Not some dainty shit, obviously.
...Jean-Noël asked me to pick up his mugwort Fleuries. That's all.

click.text: Funny seeing you behind a counter selling cigs. Thought you'd still be nicking 'em.

response.text: Huh. Not in a... err... padded room, then?
Good start. Still a little bitch, I see.

options.text: Do I see a rosary bracelet?

response.text: Yeah. Cool one. Heavy beads, solid grip. Church-approved stress ball, as Jean-Noël says.

options.text: So you hang out with the church now?

response.text: *sigh*
...As you probably remember, a couple of years ago the cops dumped me there for community service. Thought I'd carry some shit around, maybe break a pew by accident, get my hours signed and fuck off.
First week I punched some idiot stealing from the offertory box. Then they had me digging graves. I fell asleep in one, woke up, chased some looters outta the cemetery...
(God's angriest little helper.)
Eventually my hours ran out, but... I dunno. There was always some shit that needed doing.
They're alright.
Smoking fucking quit ME. Real men breathe air and trouble, not that weak shit.

options.text: So you're a good boy now?

response.text: That's disgusting. But yeah, sort of. Trying to be.
I piss myself off less these days.

options.text: What did your boss ask you to buy?

response.text: Those flowery ones. Mugwort something... Fleuries.

checkout.text: I'm leaving today. Took a shift on a trawler to make some money before the weather turns to shit.

break.text: ...Oh. The typewriter. Félix really did get me one. Cool.
Guess that means I can try those puzzles in the paper now.

entry.text: Hey, guess what I just saw.
There's a seal. Like, on the pavement, near the soup truck. Just lying there... And it's perfect.
Some of the fishermen saw it first. Said it's not scared, not hurt. Just... there.
I ran into Eel Lady down at the docks and she said I could take a few fish if I brought her some chewing tobacco. So yeah. This, please.

click.text: Sorry, Gail. Seal first. Gossip later.

response.text: Chewing tobacco. For Eel Lady.

wrong_items.text: Oh, could you also add a couple of newspapers? To wrap the fish. Maybe... three? Better too many than not enough, right?

wrong_items_wrap.text: Chewing tobacco and three newspapers, Gail. If you're forgetting too, we're doomed.

checkout.text: Okay. Fish, tobacco, newspaper. Now I gotta run, see you later!

entry.text: Hi, {{name_mado}}.

response.text: ...Not even close. Menthol Morleys, please.
Oh. Yeah, right.
...Madeleine, by the way. You can call me Mado.
Please no. If I hear that name one more time, I swear... *sigh* This town's obsessed.
Mhm. Mum loves them.
Finally, someone thought of the cake first. I've heard "Mary Magdalene" more this month than my whole life. This town's obsessed.
...Not even close. Menthol Morleys, please.
...Hmph. Cool. Menthol Morleys. Please.
Hospital. I'm here for my training year.
(Ha, knew it. Serious face. Loud heels. Of course she's not local.)
Haven't even stepped inside yet. Not sure I care to. Got enough organs of my own to deal with.
Menthol Morleys. Seriously?

entry.text: Good evening, {{name_yves}}. Mind if I hang around a bit? Waiting on Félix.
Called it a day a little early to see what he's cooked up for tonight. His plans rarely end well, but they're never boring.
Even told me to bring the trombone tonight. Would never miss it.

response.text: So far so good. The airflow's coming along. Give it a week and that part should be breathing properly again.
Then come the nerves and limbs - keys, pedals, all the fiddly bits - which I conveniently leave to my colleague's better suited pianist fingers.
This organ drains time and energy like nothing else, but still, give us two weeks or so, and the town gets back their favourite little monster.
...Why not? Fewer eyes on you, less chatter in the pews. Maybe that's it.
Or maybe it's just the air at night... Same wood, same tools, but they answer you differently after dark.
...Can't say why. Maybe there's no why.
(Alright. Let's pull that thread.)
Couldn't it have been prevented? I heard bellows are often the first thing to go. Problematic part.
...Most irritating to check.
...Bellows are a pain, yeah. And in case of this particular organ, what was the point anyway?
The whole left half was a mess - pipes knocked out or missing, the case going soft with rot. Pedals warped and stiff. Keyboard too - half the keys loose, a few straight-up gone.
So... yeah. The bellows had plenty wrong with them, but they weren't what finished the organ. Whole thing was dying already.
And you helped it die faster?

Helped it die? I did every bloody check they asked for, filled out every repair request nice and proper, just how the diocese wants them. Told them it was falling apart and needed proper repairs, not patch jobs and prayers.
No reaction. Nothing changed.
Eventually I stopped checking it properly. Just looked at the parts you could see without crawling in all the way. Figured if they didn't care, why should I?

options.text: So you cracked first, like a loser?

response.text: ...Good Lord. And you had time to think before saying that.

options.text: Sounds like weak glutes to me

response.text: ...Good Lord. And you had time to think before saying that.
...Good Lord. And you had time to think before saying that.
*sigh*
Well. Maybe I could've done my job better.
...I'll take it off the repair cost. Not much, but fair's fair.
You can be really nasty, huh?

entry.text: Evening, sunshines. How about we close up?

decor_outOfBin.text: Did you loot that out of some fairground rubbish heap?
Says the man who furnished half his flat from heaps.
Well. Low standards and an exceptional taste have always been among my strengths.
I like it, for the record. Nicely done.

decor_badTaste.text: Atrocious, cheerful, and hurting the eyes in a very festive way. Well done.
Basically your taste in one sentence.
Ha. Small minds never get it, do they?

decor_uglyHome.text: Well. That's got... just the right kind of domestic ugliness to it, I must say.
You're just too old and dusty to appreciate a good ugly interior.

end.text: Perfect. Grab the key. Time to lock up this fine establishment.

start.text: Right. The plan. The plan is simple.
Father Jean-Noël needs a grave dug, but his skinhead shovel knight is off playing sailor. So I offered to help. Figured I'd bring Yves along to make it feel like a party.
Ah. Manual labor and morbid brass. How can I say no.
And maybe a bottle of church wine if we charm him right. It is Friday, after all.

options.text: Take a look at the seal

response.text: Then follow the sound of Erika's voice. Can't miss it.

options.text: Go bother Erika if I find her

response.text: Then look somewhere near the seal. Can't miss it.
Sooodoku and siiilence, dear. Got your knitting too?
...Jeepers. Easy there.

d2bye_yvesFish.text: Mademoiselle said her name is Fish. As in Félicia.

d2end_outro2seal.text: Gail wandered through the town square, then the park, then down to the docks. She never found the seal, just sky, sea, and gulls. That was enough.

d2end_outro2erika.text: Gail checked Erika's house. Then the back of the post office, where the newspaper team hides. Erika wasn't anywhere, but the Friday buzz of pubs and cafés wasn't too bad either.

d2end_outro2sudoku.text: Sudoku always calmed Gail down, even when her hand filled the numbers almost without thinking.
Her pencil broke near the end. She couldn't find a single sharpener that hadn't been taken apart years ago. But the last few numbers were obvious, anyway.

d2end_outro2brood.text: Gail spent the evening poking old scars, staring at the ceiling, and quietly reconsidering her entire life.
Then she got bored and fell asleep.
